dialogue.content: （今日はよろしくお願いします。時間になりましたら始めさせていただきます。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for coming today. We'll begin at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.content: こちらこそよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: こんにちは相談員です。はじめに年齢性別を教えてください。
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm a counselor. To start, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: 近地には14歳女子です。
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm a 14-year-old girl.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。今日はどんなご相談ですか？
dialogue.English: Hello. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 体について悩んでる
dialogue.English: I'm worried about my body.

dialogue.content: 体についてお悩みなのですね。たとえばどんなことでお悩みですか？
dialogue.English: I see, you're concerned about your body. For example, what kinds of things are on your mind?

dialogue.content: 最近胸が膨らんできて…それが嫌だしなんでって思ってる
dialogue.English: Lately, my chest has started to develop... and I hate it, and I'm wondering why this is happening.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。最近胸が膨らんできて、嫌だなって思ってしまうんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. Your chest has started to develop recently, and it's making you feel upset.

dialogue.content: うん男とか女とか考えた事なかったけど自分は、男だって思ってたし…
dialogue.English: Yeah... I never really thought about being a boy or a girl, but I always thought of myself as a boy...

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。今までは自分は男だっていう感覚できたのですね。それは戸惑いますね。
dialogue.English: I see. So up until now, you've had the sense that you're a boy. That must be confusing.

dialogue.content: もやもやするし嫌な気持ちになる…
dialogue.English: I feel uneasy and it's an awful feeling...

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、嫌だし、もやもやするんだね。確かに今まで男と思っていたら、違和感感じるよね。
dialogue.English: I hear you—you feel uneasy and unsettled. If you've thought of yourself as a boy, it's natural to feel a sense of discomfort.

dialogue.content: そんな感じかな…
dialogue.English: Yeah, something like that...

dialogue.content: 確かに急に体の変化が見えると、びっくりするよね。嫌な気持ちにもなるよね。
dialogue.English: It's definitely surprising when you suddenly see changes in your body. It's natural that it would make you feel upset, too.

dialogue.content: だから制服も着たくない
dialogue.English: That's why I don't want to wear my uniform.

dialogue.content: うん、そうだよね。制服も違和感あるよね。なかなか受け止められないのはあたりまえだと思いますよ。
dialogue.English: Yes, I understand. The uniform must feel strange, too. I think it's perfectly normal to find it hard to accept.

dialogue.content: そうなのかなぁ？
dialogue.English: You think so?

dialogue.content: うん、そう思いますよ。
dialogue.English: Yes, I think so.

dialogue.content: なら良かった
dialogue.English: That's a relief.

dialogue.content: うん。自分の感覚を大事にすることは、とても大切だと思います。
dialogue.English: Yes. I think it's very important to honor your own feelings.

dialogue.content: ありがとう
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: うん、大事にしていいと思う。今実際に生活していて、何か困ったことは起きてない？
dialogue.English: Yes, I think it's good to cherish them. In your daily life now, is there anything that's been troubling you?

dialogue.content: 制服着たりすると吐き気がしたりしんどい
dialogue.English: When I wear my uniform, I feel nauseous and exhausted.

dialogue.content: だから学校も行きたくない
dialogue.English: That's why I don't want to go to school either.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね。。吐き気を感じたり、体もしんどくなるのですか。。それはきついね。しんどいね。
dialogue.English: I see. You feel nauseous and physically exhausted... That must be so difficult. That sounds very hard on you.

dialogue.content: 話せる人もいない
dialogue.English: I don't have anyone to talk to about it.

dialogue.content: そうだよね、なかなか話せないよね。辛いね。それは女性用の制服や下着をつけたりとか、女性性を感じるものに触れた時、いつも感じるのかな？
dialogue.English: I can imagine it's difficult to talk about. That must be painful. Do you tend to feel this way whenever you wear the girls' uniform or underwear, or when you come into contact with things that feel feminine?

dialogue.content: そうかも女物の下着や衣類全般とかそういうの全部かな…
dialogue.English: Maybe, yeah—girls' underwear and clothing in general, all of that, I think...

dialogue.content: そうなんだね。日本の中はまだ割と、男物、女物みたいな分け方もまだまだ多いから、そういうシーンも多いものね。それは本当にしんどいね。
dialogue.English: I see. In Japan, things are still often divided into men's and women's categories, so you encounter that a lot. That must be really exhausting.

dialogue.content: かなりしんどい…
dialogue.English: It's really exhausting...

dialogue.content: いつ頃から感じ始めたのですか？今まで耐えてきてしんどかったね。
dialogue.English: When did you start to feel this way? It must have been so hard to endure it all this time.

dialogue.content: 中学校になってからかなそれまでは制服もなかったからなんとも思わなかった
dialogue.English: I think since I started junior high. Before that, we didn't have uniforms, so I never really thought about it.

dialogue.content: そうだよね。小学生なら服装とは自由だもんね。
dialogue.English: That's right. In elementary school, you're free to wear what you want.

dialogue.content: スカートとかはかなかったし
dialogue.English: I never wore skirts or anything like that.

dialogue.content: では今は毎日制服着ないといけない環境できつすぎるね。
dialogue.English: So now, being in an environment where you have to wear a uniform every day must be too much for you.

dialogue.content: だから学校も行きたくない
dialogue.English: That's why I don't want to go to school.

dialogue.content: そう思ってしまうよね。
dialogue.English: It's understandable to feel that way.

dialogue.content: うん…
dialogue.English: Yeah...

dialogue.content: 本当はどうならいいなあって思ったことはある？
dialogue.English: Have you ever thought about how you would ideally like things to be?

dialogue.content: 男も女もなくなればいいと思ってる…
dialogue.English: I wish there were no such things as male or female...

dialogue.content: うん、そう思うよね。そういう区別なくなるといいよね。
dialogue.English: I hear you. It would be nice if those distinctions disappeared.

dialogue.content: 区別する意味ってなんかあるの？
dialogue.English: Is there any point in making those distinctions?

dialogue.content: 肉体的な区別だけだと思うんだけどね。生物学的に男性の方が力が強かったり体が大きくなりやすかったり、生殖器の形状が違ったりするだけで。
dialogue.English: I believe it's only a physical distinction. Biologically, males tend to be stronger or grow larger, and the shape of their reproductive organs is different, but that's it.

dialogue.content: でもみんな男とか女で区分したがるし学校とかは特にそうじゃない？
dialogue.English: But everyone wants to categorize people as male or female, and that's especially true at school, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 本当だよね。ずーっと先生たちは、明治時代からのやり方を変えないでいるような気がします。
dialogue.English: That's very true. I feel like teachers have been sticking to the same old ways since the Meiji era.

dialogue.content: よくネットとかでも関係ないとか言うけど全然そんなんじゃないし
dialogue.English: People on the internet often say it doesn't matter, but that's not how it is in reality at all.

dialogue.content: 確かに、実際は理想はそうだけど現実はまだまだ変わらないと思うこともまだまだ多いよね。でも今は少しずつ変わってきているんですよ。知っているかもしれないけど、女子の制服がズボンを選択できたり、同性同士の結婚を認める自治体も増えてきているんですよ。
dialogue.English: It's true, while that might be the ideal, there are still many times when it feels like reality isn't changing. But things are starting to change, little by little. You may already know this, but some schools now allow girls to choose trousers for their uniform, and more municipalities are recognizing same-sex marriage.

dialogue.content: だけど自分のとこは制服選べないし選べたとしても変な目で見られそうで怖い
dialogue.English: But at my school, we can't choose our uniform, and even if we could, I'm scared of getting weird looks.

dialogue.content: 確かにそう思ってしまうよね。
dialogue.English: It's understandable to feel that way.

dialogue.content: 親もわかってくれないし辛い…
dialogue.English: My parents don't understand either, and it's painful...

dialogue.content: そうだよね、親にはわかってほしい気がするよね。
dialogue.English: I know. You really want your parents to understand, don't you?

dialogue.content: いずれは変わるから大丈夫ってちゃんと聞いてくれない…
dialogue.English: They just say, “Things will change eventually, it'll be fine,” and don't really listen...

dialogue.content: そうなんだ、言ったことはあるんだね。言ってもその時は変わらなかったのですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so you have told them before. But even when you did, nothing changed at the time.

dialogue.content: うんまた言ってもわかってくれないから言いたくないしどうすればいいかわかんない…
dialogue.English: Yeah... they won't understand even if I tell them again, so I don't want to. I don't know what to do...

dialogue.content: そうだよね。なんて説明していいかわからなくなるよね。悩んじゃうよね。でもね、あなたは一人じゃないからね。いつでも相談員は話を聞くからね。
dialogue.English: I understand. It becomes hard to know how to explain it. It's really weighing on you. But please know, you are not alone. I am always here to listen.

dialogue.content: ありがとう…1人で考えてたけどやっぱりどうすればいいかわかんなくて…
dialogue.English: Thank you... I've been thinking about it by myself, but I really don't know what to do...

dialogue.content: 世の中におそらくあなたみたいな悩みで、悩んでる人って実はすごく多いんです。言わないだけでね。
dialogue.English: There are probably a lot of people in the world struggling with the same worries you have. They just don't talk about it.

dialogue.content: そうなんだ知らなかった…
dialogue.English: Really? I didn't know that...

dialogue.content: そして気軽に話せる内容じゃないことも理解しているのでいつでも相談に来ていいのですよ。相談内容はここからは絶対に漏れることもないので安心してください。
dialogue.English: And I understand that this isn't an easy thing to talk about, so you can come to me anytime. Please rest assured that whatever we discuss here will be kept completely confidential.

dialogue.content: ありがとう…1人じゃないって思ったら少し楽になった。
dialogue.English: Thank you... It feels a little easier knowing I'm not alone.

dialogue.content: はい、あなたは一人じゃありませんから。今日は残念ながら時間になってしまいましたが、いかがでしたか？また何か相談したり辛いときは来てくださいね。
dialogue.English: That's right, you are not alone. Unfortunately, our time is up for today, but how are you feeling? Please come back anytime you want to talk or if things get tough.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。またキツくなったら話聞いてください。
dialogue.English: Thank you. Please listen to me again when things get hard.

dialogue.content: いつでも来てくださいね。（今日はありがとうございました。ここで終了させていただきます。）
dialogue.English: Please come back anytime. (Thank you for your time today. We'll end the session here.)
